messages:
alex: Heads-up — drafted a lightweight design for a deprecation-signal queue + feature-flag gating for shims. Goal: decouple runtime header checks from heavy shim logic and give us a safe rollout path. Wanted quick feedback before I turn it into an RFC.

zara: Nice. high-level: queue receives 'deprecation events' (tenant, api, header, timestamp, severity) and we evaluate per-request whether to apply shim. That avoids per-request DB lookups. :+1:

alex: Exactly. Two modes: realtime (short TTL in cache for fast on/off) and batched (periodic sync for bulk changes). Tunable TTL per-tenant.

tomas: Concern: ordering/race between enqueue and clients that already got a cached decision. How do we ensure fast rollbacks?

alex: Plan: make cache entries have an explicit "applied_at" and a short grace TTL (30s) then a safer longer TTL (5m) that can be invalidated by an explicit purge event. Purge events push to the same queue.

li: Telemetry note — we need per-decision metadata emitted so we can correlate shim-on vs shim-off with error-rate and latency. Suggest adding tags: "signal_source", "decision_version", "rule_id".

ashley: Rollout strategy idea: target 0% -> 1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% over N minutes, with automatic rollback if error-rate spike > X% or latency P95 regresses by Y ms. Canary should be per-region and per-tenant.

kevin: What about tenants with sticky routing? If a tenant is pinned to a Dedicated pool we might need a different TTL / immediate effect - can't rely on eventual sync.

alex: Good catch. We'll allow tenant-level policy overrides: "immediate": true for dedicated/high-priority customers. That bypasses the cache and applies shim in-process (still emits events so we can audit).

zara: Implementation sketch — event schema + sample flag config:```json
{
  "rule_id": "deprecated-header-x",
  "match": {"header": "X-RW-OLD", "present": true},
  "action": "apply_shim",
  "rollout": {"percent": 10},
  "ttl_seconds": 300
}
```

tomas: Storage/backing queue? SQS? Kafka? Prefer something with strong ordering per-tenant to handle purge/overrides.

alex: Leaning Kafka (or PubSub with ordering keys) — we need low-latency fanout to edge caches. We'll write a small service that consumes and fanouts invalidation events to edge nodes via a push channel.

li: Metrics list: decision_count, decision_breakdown_by_rule, shim_applied_rate, shim_error_rate, decision_latency. Also include sampling of raw requests for debugging when a rule flips.

kevin: Does this change our contract with SDKs / clients? We need to document that header semantics might be transformed by server-side shims under a rollout flag.

alex: We'll add a deprecation-policy header we emit when shim is applied: X-RW-Deprecation: rule=deprecated-header-x;applied=true;ver=3. Clients can opt in to see that.

ashley: Ops/Playbook: add an emergency cutoff that immediately disables all non-critical shims across the fleet (killing queue consumers). Also add a TTL-based self-heal so stale cache entries don't lock things for > TTL.

zara: One more tradeoff: If we centralize decisions, we reduce duplicated logic but add a single control-plane dependency. Might be fine if the edge has local fallback rules. Suggest we keep a small fallback table baked into edge binary for most common rules.

alex: Agreed — plan: authoritative control-plane via queue + local fallback table for critical shims. Fallback table updated by config releases.

kevin: Anything for auditing / customer requests? Tenants will ask for history of when a shim was applied.

li: Event store should retain deprecation events 90 days and we export per-tenant timelines to the console. Also attach decision_version so we can replay.

alex: Next steps: I'll turn this into an RFC with the schema, lifecycle, and a proposed rollout playbook. If nobody objects, I'll file by end of week. Ping me with specific objections.

zara: SGTM, add a short section on cost (fanout QPS) and estimated added SLOs for control-plane latency.

ashley: Add runbook snippet for rollback: // emergency disable consumer; clear edge caches; set global flag disabled=true; monitor 5m

ops-bot: deploy-bot: consumer-service version v0.6 deployed to staging at 2024-09-12T16:12:31Z :rocket:

tomas: Thanks all — will leave comments in the RFC when it's up.
